Interior of a "Seascape Haven", a medium-scale, rectangular, cubic orientation residential space with a gently sloping pitched ceiling. The room is bathed in bright, natural daylight streaming through rectangular windows that offer coastal views. The walls are clad in weathered, sun-bleached wooden planks with a natural, sandy texture, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere. A street-level, ultra-wide photograph of the Habitation Blocks in Neo-Kyoto, captured from a slightly elevated position (25-30° downward tilt). Towering, utilitarian Brutalist residential blocks, constructed from weathered, grimy concrete stained with streaks, dominate the frame, forming a narrow, canyon-like street. These aged facades are augmented with prominent, rounded, smooth white composite living pods projecting outwards, their large, curved windows emitting a warm, inviting orange glow that reveals glimpses of furniture and art within. The narrow street below is perpetually damp asphalt, reflecting scattered artificial streetlights that cast pools of stark light and deep shadows. Several yellow, boxy, futuristic vehicles, resembling taxis or delivery vans, traverse the wet surface. Balconies on the older parts of the buildings are cluttered with an assortment of items: potted plants, tables, and salvaged equipment, creating a lived-in, chaotic yet functional atmosphere. In the distant background, formidable, spiky skyscrapers pierce through a pervasive, hazy, overcast sky, suggesting a more imposing sector of the metropolis. The lighting is low and diffused, with pockets of warm orange glow from the pods contrasting sharply with the muted grays and browns of the concrete and the stark artificial lights. Rusted metal railings and grimy glass windows add to the worn texture of the scene. The overall mood is one of resilient, lived-in grit and a slightly melancholic beauty, capturing the working-class inhabitants' adaptation to a dense megacity. The composition is asymmetric, with the building entrance visible but not centered, shot at a slight angle to emphasize depth and dimension, and more street visible on one side, avoiding any perfect symmetry.
